sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that there are material improvements in the statements made by the victim as well as her sister.
He further submits that though the prosecution has placed on record the FSL report, the same, however, does not connect the appellant with the foetus.
He further submits that the appellant's name was not even taken at the time of recording of MLC or the statement recorded under Section 164 of the victim's sister.
Lastly, he submits that though the victim has been shown to be recovered from the possession of the appellant at Ghaziabad, the arrest memo does not reflect the place of arrest at Ghaziabad.
4. Learned APP for the State, duly assisted by learned Amicus Curiae appointed to represent the victim, opposes the present application.
It is submitted that the victim was 14 years and 7 months old at the time of incident and she alongwith her younger sister were taken away by the appellant to Ghaziabad.
The victim's sister, aged about 8 years, also supported the aforesaid fact of being taken away by the appellant.
5. The nominal roll of the appellant has been placed on record as per which, he has undergone about 7 years.
6. In view of the above and having gone through the testimony of victim as well as her previous statements, I find no ground to entertain the present application at this stage.
Accordingly, the same is dismissed with liberty to move an application an application at the appropriate stage.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 04/12/2025 at 21:06:14 1.

Learned APP for the State, on instructions, submits that the victim was a child victim and pregnant and the conviction has been rendered under Section 6 of POCSO Act, however, the victim has been awarded only compensation of Rs.10.5 lakhs whereas as the maximum awardable amount is Rs.16.5 lakhs.

2. Let a copy of this order be communicated to the Member Secretary, DSLSA, Rouse Avenue who shall take steps to ensure that the maximum awardable compensation amount is disbursed to the victim as per Delhi Victim Compensation Scheme.
The I.O. will facilitate the victim/family members in approaching the Member Secretary, DSLSA to do the needful.
3. List in due course.
MANOJ KUMAR OHRI, J DECEMBER 1, 2025 na
